method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

sourceChecks.note: Opened and searched: preparation intolerance requires contact; sedative transport restrictions; fever/severe pain need immediate care. US screening-age content was not imported.
Opened/searched urgent warning section: breathing difficulty and worsening chest/abdominal pain. Item029 swallowing-recovery protocol itself not verified by this page excerpt.
Page opened but targeted symptom search did not expose the relevant passages. Core bleeding-risk inference clinically reviewed; no claim of complete external validation.
Opened/found complications and seek-care section: pancreatitis, bleeding/perforation and severe pain/vomiting warrant assessment.
ACR/RSNA page opened and implant section examined: device screening and compatibility precautions before entering the scanner room.

items.assessment: Repeated vomiting/incomplete prep needs individualized procedural advice. Independent substitution, unreported omission and faster intake are plausible but unsafe completion shortcuts; source explicitly instructs contact for prep intolerance.
The red flags are correct, but offering food is unrelated and routine follow-up is a weak competing response.
issues: The red flags are correct, but offering food is unrelated and routine follow-up is a weak competing response.

options: Use the routine postprocedure advice for mild gas pain and reassess after rest
Arrange urgent clinical assessment
Encourage walking for presumed retained gas only
Give the prescribed analgesic and antipyretic before deciding whether further assessment is needed
why: Worsening pain with fever exceeds expected transient bloating and warrants urgent assessment.
These findings can indicate a significant procedural complication.
Fever with worsening pain is not routine gas discomfort.
Symptom relief must not postpone evaluation of possible perforation or other complication.

items.assessment: Perceived alertness, normal BP, walking and caffeine are credible but insufficient proxies for psychomotor recovery. Apply the actual discharge restrictions and safe transport plan.
Swallowing/recovery criterion is correct; completion of paperwork is irrelevant to physiological readiness.
issues: Swallowing/recovery criterion is correct; completion of paperwork is irrelevant to physiological readiness.

options: The client's report of thirst alone
Absence of abdominal pain
A fixed interval after the procedure without checking recovery of throat sensation or swallowing
Recovery criteria and swallowing safety per protocol
why: Thirst does not establish recovery of safe swallowing.
Abdominal comfort does not assess pharyngeal sensation.
Elapsed time alone is insufficient; follow protocol recovery criteria and assess swallowing safety.
Pharyngeal anaesthesia can temporarily impair airway protection.

items.assessment: Contrasts mild improving expected symptoms with new breathing difficulty or severe persistent pain. The source directly supports the warning signs. No competing answers found.
Current shock-type cues after biopsy support bleeding; meal and next-day options are cartoon distractors. Use clinically plausible cause/response alternatives.
issues: Current shock-type cues after biopsy support bleeding; meal and next-day options are cartoon distractors. Use clinically plausible cause/response alternatives.

options: Give the prescribed analgesic and repeat vital signs at the routine interval before notifying the team
Urgently assess and escalate possible bleeding
Treat the lightheadedness as residual sedation because the biopsy dressing is dry
Assess whether the client can stand before deciding if the blood-pressure drop is significant
why: Analgesia alone risks delaying response to worsening pain with circulatory deterioration.
The combined findings suggest clinically important haemorrhage.
A dry dressing does not exclude internal bleeding and the combined trend needs urgent assessment.
Mobilization is unsafe while possible circulatory compromise is being assessed.

items.assessment: Key is appropriate, but fasting reversing anticoagulation is an implausible mechanism.
issues: Key is appropriate, but fasting reversing anticoagulation is an implausible mechanism.

options: Notify the procedural team before proceeding
Record the medicine and proceed because the most recent haemoglobin is normal
Tell the client to stop it for a week independently
Add the anticoagulant to the medication list without alerting the procedural team
why: Anticoagulant exposure changes bleeding-risk planning.
Normal haemoglobin does not establish that the anticoagulant-related procedure risk has been addressed.
Interruption requires a clinician-directed balance of bleeding and clotting risk.
Updating a list alone may not communicate the time-sensitive bleeding-risk change.

items.assessment: Retention assessment is correct; several litres quickly and every change normal are exaggerated.
issues: Retention assessment is correct; several litres quickly and every change normal are exaggerated.

options: Use the routine advice for mild burning and wait for symptoms to settle
Continue encouraging usual fluids without checking bladder distension or output
Arrange a routine urine culture and defer bladder assessment until the sample is obtained
Promptly assess and contact the procedural team
why: Painful inability to void differs from expected transient irritation.
The suspected retention/obstruction needs assessment rather than hydration advice alone.
Inability to void with pain requires timely assessment; inability to provide a sample is part of the concern.
Painful inability to void may indicate retention or obstruction.

items.assessment: ERCP severe persistent pain/vomiting is a useful pattern, but large meal and fasting-only assumptions make the key obvious.
issues: ERCP severe persistent pain/vomiting is a useful pattern, but large meal and fasting-only assumptions make the key obvious.

options: Give the prescribed antiemetic and assess only whether the vomiting stops
Discharge because the procedure report was normal
Escalate for assessment of a complication
Apply routine advice for transient post-endoscopy bloating without reviewing the pain pattern
why: The severe persistent abdominal pain also needs prompt complication assessment.
A normal procedural report does not exclude later complications.
Pancreatitis and other complications require prompt evaluation.
Severe persistent pain with vomiting is beyond expected mild transient bloating.

items.assessment: Vital trends/internal bleeding assessment are appropriate; eating ability is unrelated to the priority.
issues: Vital trends/internal bleeding assessment are appropriate; eating ability is unrelated to the priority.

options: Assess only the puncture-site dressing and pain at its surface
Vital signs and their change from baseline
Abdominal discomfort and evidence of bleeding
Only whether the dressing remains dry
why: A local surface check alone can miss internal bleeding and impaired perfusion.
A trend can reveal impaired perfusion after biopsy.
These findings help assess a procedural bleeding complication.
A dry surface dressing does not exclude internal bleeding.

items.assessment: Actual prior wheeze/facial swelling with contrast is the important exposure history; seafood labelling, spontaneous resolution and unauthorized self-premedication do not resolve risk. No regimen is prescribed independently.
New renal decline should be communicated, but cancelling all future imaging is implausibly absolute.
issues: New renal decline should be communicated, but cancelling all future imaging is implausibly absolute.

options: Assume last month's creatinine remains sufficient
Use an old normal result because the contrast order has already been signed
Start extra hydration without reviewing the prescribed fluid restriction
Communicate the change to the imaging team
why: An acute change makes the older result less relevant.
The imaging team must know about a new renal change before weighing current risks and benefits.
Hydration decisions must be individualized to current kidney and cardiac/fluid status.
Current renal status may alter imaging and hydration decisions.

items.assessment: Unknown implant identity is a concrete MRI stop-and-verify issue; recent manufacture, absent magnet symptoms and removing jewellery cannot establish conditions. ACR/RSNA source supports screening before exposure.
Early support planning is right; another person’s sedative is an obviously unsafe non-option.
issues: Early support planning is right; another person’s sedative is an obviously unsafe non-option.

options: Promise the scan will be brief without checking
Notify the team early and plan support
Wait until the scan begins to discuss it
Arrange a sedative for the morning of the scan without checking radiology instructions, monitoring or transport
why: Inaccurate reassurance can undermine informed preparation.
Preparation allows individualized strategies or ordered medication planning.
Late disclosure limits preparation options.
Medication support needs coordinated authorization and a safe procedural/recovery plan.

items.assessment: Pregnancy screening/communication is right; no nausea and permanent cancellation are unrealistic contrasts.
issues: Pregnancy screening/communication is right; no nausea and permanent cancellation are unrealistic contrasts.

options: Follow screening policy and notify the imaging team
Use a previous negative pregnancy test as clearance without checking timing or current history
Automatically defer every radiographic examination until after delivery
Proceed without communicating because exposure is brief
why: Pregnancy status may affect imaging decisions and preparation.
A past result may not reflect current pregnancy possibility; apply the current screening policy.
Necessary imaging requires an individualized clinical risk-benefit decision, not universal deferral.
The team needs relevant pregnancy information regardless of duration.

items.assessment: Order-conflict clarification is correct; another client’s instructions are unrelated to this client’s authorized plan.
issues: Order-conflict clarification is correct; another client’s instructions are unrelated to this client’s authorized plan.

options: Choose whichever instruction is newest without checking
Apply a universal midnight-fast rule
Ask a colleague to choose the fasting rule they usually use for that procedure
Clarify with the procedural team before intake
why: The new order may not account for the planned procedure.
Fasting requirements vary by procedure and anaesthetic plan.
Habit does not resolve the specific contradictory instructions; clarify with the responsible team.
Procedure-specific fasting requirements need a consistent plan.

items.assessment: Accessible cues are important, but shouting from behind and removing every aid are conspicuous errors.
issues: Accessible cues are important, but shouting from behind and removing every aid are conspicuous errors.

options: Give louder verbal instructions without checking whether the client can distinguish them
Explain the instructions only after sedation
Agree on accessible cues before starting
Remove a hearing aid needed for the procedure without agreeing on an alternative cue
why: Volume alone does not establish reliable communication for time-sensitive breath cues.
Sedation may reduce comprehension and recall.
Reliable communication supports cooperation during time-sensitive instructions.
If an aid must be removed, an accessible alternative must be established before starting.

items.assessment: Documenting a known chronic asymmetry and current neurological baseline enables interpretation after sedation. This is a specific preprocedure safety purpose; no automatic cancellation rule is imposed.
A previous blistering antiseptic reaction needs clarification and team planning before exposure. Less product, improvised barrier cream or absent current rash do not establish tolerance.
Difficulty staying awake warrants immediate respiratory/alertness assessment, not merely generic continued monitoring. Food and fictional recovery documentation are weak distractors.
issues: Difficulty staying awake warrants immediate respiratory/alertness assessment, not merely generic continued monitoring. Food and fictional recovery documentation are weak distractors.

options: Discharge if a relative promises close observation
Allow extra sleep without checking respiratory depth, rate or responsiveness
Use the elapsed recovery time as the main criterion because the procedure was uncomplicated
Assess airway, breathing and responsiveness, continue monitoring and urgently escalate unmet recovery criteria
why: Home supervision does not replace adequate immediate recovery.
Persistent sedation can impair ventilation and requires active assessment.
The client’s current recovery and physiological state determine readiness.
Persistent difficulty arousing can indicate significant sedation effects; immediate assessment and appropriate help take priority over discharge timing.

items.assessment: Increasing bleeding plus dyspnoea is the discriminating cue; thirst and discharge scheduling are irrelevant options.
issues: Increasing bleeding plus dyspnoea is the discriminating cue; thirst and discharge scheduling are irrelevant options.

options: A single small blood streak immediately after airway instrumentation
A mild sore throat that improves while the client rests
Increasing bleeding with respiratory symptoms
The mere presence of any cough
why: A small isolated streak can occur, unlike progressive bleeding with dyspnoea.
Improving local irritation is less concerning than new progressive bleeding and respiratory symptoms.
The new pattern suggests a complication needing urgent assessment.
Some coughing can occur after airway instrumentation.

items.assessment: Positional post-lumbar-puncture headache pattern is meaningful; disbelief and immediate prolonged walking are poor distractors.
issues: Positional post-lumbar-puncture headache pattern is meaningful; disbelief and immediate prolonged walking are poor distractors.

Assess and report the positional pattern
Diagnose migraine without further assessment
Document only the pain score while the client is lying comfortably
why: A clear postural/procedural pattern needs assessment and communication rather than assumption.
The pattern helps identify a postprocedural headache and guide treatment.
The temporal and positional features require procedure-related evaluation.
The positional change is essential information and should not be omitted because resting pain improves.

items.assessment: The unilateral post-thoracentesis respiratory change is useful, but meal/recheck is unrelated filler.
issues: The unilateral post-thoracentesis respiratory change is useful, but meal/recheck is unrelated filler.

options: Activate urgent assessment for a respiratory complication
Encourage repeated forceful coughing first

scopeNote: Clinical recognition is not a complete procedural protocol. All modified items need independent post-revision review; unlisted procedural details were not exhaustively source-checked.
